name: Vacuum suction wrinkle treatment (1932)

lead: In 1932 a suction treatment was presented in the popular press as a way to clean the skin and, according to a later account of Modern Mechanix coverage, to suck the wrinkles out. It belongs to early-20th-century vacuum beauty devices that aimed at smoother-looking skin.
Very little documentation survives about the specific device, its maker or its method.

paras: Suction was applied to the face through a cup or vacuum tip, an approach that also appears in earlier products such as earlier suction-cup products.
No risks are documented for this specific device; mild suction can bruise or irritate skin.

Wrinkles claimed to be pulled out
angle.text: The treatment was advertised to smooth wrinkles by pulling on the skin and cleansing it. It is documented as period marketing, with no known study.

lead: The 1932 suction treatment was a vacuum-based skin-care procedure pictured in Modern Mechanix and reproduced by Collectors Weekly as a 1932 suction treatment for skin cleaning, one that claimed to pull wrinkles out of the skin [1]. The goal was smoother, cleaner-looking facial skin.

It sits among other vacuum beauty devices of the era, including the 1941 Glamour Bonnet, which was claimed to improve the complexion by reducing air pressure around the head [1]. Details such as the inventor and mechanism are not given in the source.

paras: Collectors Weekly describes a vacuum procedure from Modern Mechanix that claimed to suck wrinkles out of the skin, and a 1932 suction treatment for skin cleaning [1]. No further mechanical detail is given [1].
Vacuum products were a recurring theme: the Glamour Bonnet (1941) reduced air pressure around the head, with its inventor believing it would improve the complexion [1].

timeline.event: Suction treatment for skin cleaning and wrinkles appears in Modern Mechanix [1].
Glamour Bonnet vacuum helmet promoted for the complexion [1].
